title: Abdominal pain in pregnancy
summary: Any abdominal, side, or pelvic pain in pregnancy — includes ruling out ectopic, ovarian cyst accident, appendicitis, abruption, UTI, and labour before reassuring round ligament pain, pelvic girdle pain, or constipation.

openingFields.label: Known risk factors (e.g. previous ectopic, IVF/assisted conception, PID, coil in situ, fibroids, known ovarian cyst)

abdo-01.text: Are there any signs of shock or collapse right now — feeling faint or dizzy, rapid heartbeat, clammy skin, confusion, or reduced consciousness?
abdo-01.phoneText: Ask: does she feel faint or dizzy, or like she might pass out? Is her heart racing?

answers.label: Yes — signs of shock or collapse

citation.section: Maternal mortality reports — collapse alongside abdominal pain as a red-flag combination

abdo-02.text: Is the pain severe and constant — not coming and going — especially if the tummy feels very hard or tense?
abdo-02.phoneText: Ask: is the pain there all the time, not easing off between spells? Does her tummy feel very hard or tight?

citation.section: GTG 63 — Antepartum Haemorrhage, placental abruption can present with pain alone (concealed abruption)

abdo-03.text: Is there any vaginal bleeding with the pain?

abdo-early-01.text: Is the pain mainly on one side, or is there any pain at the tip of the shoulder?
abdo-early-01.phoneText: Ask: is the pain mostly on one side, or does she have any pain right up at the shoulder tip?

citation.section: Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage — presenting symptoms of ectopic pregnancy

abdo-early-01b.text: Was the pain sudden in onset and severe, especially on one side, possibly with nausea or vomiting — particularly if there's a known ovarian cyst, fibroid, or she's had fertility treatment?
abdo-early-01b.phoneText: Ask: did the pain come on suddenly and badly, mostly on one side? Is she feeling or being sick with it? Does she know of an ovarian cyst?

abdo-early-02.text: Is the pain in the lower right side of the tummy, together with loss of appetite, nausea or vomiting, or a temperature?
abdo-early-02.phoneText: Ask: is the pain low down on the right? Has she gone off her food, felt sick, or had a temperature?

abdo-early-03.text: Any fever, pain or burning when passing urine, or needing to pass urine more often than usual?

abdo-early-03b.text: Does this sound like constipation — bloating, straining, infrequent or hard stools, with nothing else concerning?

abdo-early-04.text: Is the pain mild to moderate, comes and goes with movement or position, and there's nothing else concerning?

answers.label: Yes — sounds like simple/round ligament pain
No — something else, or she's still worried

abdo-later-01.text: Are the pains regular tightenings, coming and going in a pattern, and getting closer together?
abdo-later-01.phoneText: Ask: do the pains come and go like tightenings, and are they getting more regular or closer together?

citation.section: Preterm labour and birth — assessment of suspected preterm labour

abdo-later-01b.text: Was the pain sudden in onset and severe, especially on one side, possibly with nausea or vomiting — particularly if there's a known ovarian cyst, fibroid, or she's had fertility treatment?
abdo-later-01b.phoneText: Ask: did the pain come on suddenly and badly, mostly on one side? Is she feeling or being sick with it? Does she know of an ovarian cyst?

abdo-later-02.text: Is there also a headache, visual disturbance (flashing lights or blurring), or pain under the ribs / epigastric pain?

citation.section: Hypertension in pregnancy — symptoms of pre-eclampsia to screen for at every contact

abdo-later-03.text: Is the pain in the lower right side of the tummy, together with loss of appetite, nausea or vomiting, or a temperature?

abdo-later-04.text: Fever, loin/flank pain, pain or burning passing urine, or needing to pass urine more often than usual (possible kidney infection)?

abdo-later-04b.text: Is the pain over the pubic bone, groin, hips, or lower back — worse walking, climbing stairs, standing on one leg, or turning over in bed, sometimes with clicking or grinding (typical of pelvic girdle pain / SPD)?
abdo-later-04b.phoneText: Ask: is it pain at the front over the pubic bone, or across the hips/lower back, that's worse walking, on stairs, or turning over in bed?

answers.label: Yes — sounds like pelvic girdle pain / SPD

abdo-later-05.text: Does this sound like constipation — bloating, straining, infrequent or hard stools, with nothing else concerning?

abdo-later-06.text: Is the pain mild, sharp or aching, worse on standing, moving, or coughing, low in the tummy or groin, with nothing else concerning (typical of round ligament/stretching pain)?

answers.label: Yes — sounds like simple/round ligament pain
No — something else, or she's still worried

abdo-outcome-red-shock.title: Abdominal pain with signs of shock or collapse
actions: Call 999 / put out an emergency call per local protocol.
Consider ectopic rupture, concealed placental abruption, ovarian cyst accident (torsion/rupture), or another acute abdominal emergency — do not wait to determine the exact cause before escalating.
Do not perform a digital vaginal examination — placenta praevia has not been excluded.
IV access, bloods including group & save/crossmatch, senior obstetric and (if not clearly obstetric) general surgical input.
See the Maternal collapse emergency drill for full A–E actions.
abdo-outcome-red-shock.phoneScript: Tell her to call 999 now — do not drive herself. Severe tummy pain with feeling faint or a racing heart in pregnancy is an emergency.
documentationPrompts: Vital signs and level of consciousness.
Time of emergency call and response.

citations.section: Maternal mortality reports — collapse as a red-flag presentation requiring immediate escalation
GTG 56 — Maternal Collapse in Pregnancy and the Puerperium

abdo-outcome-red-severepain.title: Severe, constant abdominal pain — suspected acute abdomen or concealed abruption
actions: Arrange immediate emergency transfer — do not wait for a routine slot.

At 24+ weeks: treat as suspected placental abruption even without visible bleeding (abruption can be concealed) — see the Vaginal bleeding pathway and Major obstetric haemorrhage drill for full actions; continuous fetal monitoring once available.

Under 24 weeks: consider ectopic pregnancy rupture, ovarian cyst accident (torsion or rupture), or another surgical abdominal emergency — arrange emergency gynaecology/surgical assessment alongside obstetric review.
Do not perform a digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia excluded.
Call 999 immediately if any signs of shock develop at any point.
abdo-outcome-red-severepain.phoneScript: Tell her this needs emergency assessment now — please call 999 or go straight to the emergency department, do not wait.
safetyNetting: Call 999 immediately if she feels faint, dizzy, or unwell on the way in.
documentationPrompts: Onset, site, and character of pain.
Fetal movements and (once available) fetal heart status.

citations.section: GTG 63 — Antepartum Haemorrhage, concealed placental abruption
Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage — presenting symptoms of ectopic pregnancy

abdo-outcome-orange-bleeding.title: Abdominal pain with vaginal bleeding
actions: Also work through the Vaginal bleeding in pregnancy pathway — treat as antepartum haemorrhage (24+ weeks) or early-pregnancy bleeding (under 24 weeks) according to gestation; the two presentations share the same red-flag causes (abruption, ectopic, praevia).
Do not perform a digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia excluded.
Arrange same-day assessment with observations, fetal assessment as appropriate for gestation, and ultrasound.
abdo-outcome-orange-bleeding.phoneScript: Tell her this needs checking today — please come in now, or call 999 if bleeding becomes heavy or she feels faint.
safetyNetting: Call 999 immediately if bleeding becomes heavy, pain worsens, or she feels faint or unwell.

abdo-outcome-red-ectopic.title: Suspected ectopic pregnancy
actions: Arrange emergency transfer for assessment — do not wait for a routine early pregnancy unit slot.
Early pregnancy unit or gynaecology emergency assessment with urgent ultrasound and beta-hCG.
If any signs of shock/collapse develop at any point, call 999 immediately.
abdo-outcome-red-ectopic.phoneScript: Tell her this needs to be checked as an emergency today — advise her to go straight to the emergency department or call 999 if the pain is severe, she feels faint, or symptoms worsen on the way.
safetyNetting: Call 999 immediately if pain becomes severe, she feels faint/dizzy, or she collapses.
documentationPrompts: Gestation / last menstrual period if known.
Advice given and route of referral.

citations.section: Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage — presenting symptoms and emergency referral

abdo-outcome-orange-ovariancyst.title: Possible ovarian cyst accident (torsion or rupture) — cannot be excluded by phone
abdo-outcome-orange-ovariancyst.target: Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / same-day emergency assessment (phone)
actions: Arrange same-day joint obstetric and gynaecology assessment — ovarian torsion is time-critical for ovary-conserving surgery, so a low threshold for review is appropriate.
Pelvic/transvaginal ultrasound with Doppler flow assessment where available, to look for an adnexal mass and assess ovarian blood flow.

If signs of shock develop at any point (suggesting rupture with bleeding), escalate immediately as a maternal emergency — see the Abdominal pain with signs of shock outcome and Maternal collapse drill.
Ovarian cysts are more common in the first trimester (e.g. corpus luteal cysts) and with assisted conception, but torsion can occur at any gestation.
abdo-outcome-orange-ovariancyst.phoneScript: Tell her this needs checking today by the maternity and gynaecology teams — please come in now. Call 999 instead if the pain becomes severe or she feels faint or very unwell.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately, any time, if pain worsens, she feels faint or dizzy, or she feels very unwell.
documentationPrompts: Known cyst/fibroid or fertility treatment history.

citations.section: Ovarian torsion/cyst accident in pregnancy — not covered by a dedicated NICE or RCOG guideline

abdo-outcome-orange-appendicitis.title: Possible appendicitis — cannot be excluded by phone
abdo-outcome-orange-appendicitis.target: Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / same-day emergency assessment (phone)
actions: Arrange same-day joint obstetric and general surgical assessment — appendicitis cannot be safely excluded remotely.

Be aware presentation is often atypical in pregnancy — as the uterus enlarges the appendix is displaced upward and laterally, so pain may not be in the classic right iliac fossa position, especially later in pregnancy — VERIFY this against a surgical reference before teaching it as fact.
Bloods (FBC, CRP) and urinalysis to help exclude a urinary cause; consider ultrasound; do not delay surgical review awaiting results.
Missed or delayed diagnosis of appendicitis in pregnancy carries higher rates of perforation and fetal loss — a low threshold for review is appropriate.
abdo-outcome-orange-appendicitis.phoneScript: Tell her this needs checking today by both the maternity and surgical teams — please come in now. Call 999 instead if the pain becomes severe or she feels very unwell.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately, any time, if pain worsens, spreads, or she develops a high fever, vomiting, or feels very unwell.
documentationPrompts: Site and character of pain, and how it has changed.

citations.section: Appendicitis in pregnancy — atypical presentation; not covered by a dedicated NICE or RCOG guideline

abdo-outcome-orange-uti.title: Possible urinary tract infection / pyelonephritis
actions: Arrange same-day assessment — urine dipstick and midstream urine sample sent for culture.

If fever, loin pain, rigors, or feeling systemically unwell: treat as suspected pyelonephritis — admit, IV antibiotics per local protocol, and consider a full sepsis screen (see Sepsis emergency drill if any red-flag features).

If lower urinary symptoms only, without fever or systemic upset: treat per local UTI-in-pregnancy protocol — VERIFY current first-line antibiotic choice locally rather than advising a specific drug here.
abdo-outcome-orange-uti.phoneScript: Tell her this needs checking today — please come in so we can test a urine sample and check for infection. If she starts shivering, feels very unwell, or breathless, call 999 instead.
safetyNetting: Call 999 if she develops shivering, confusion, rapid breathing, or feels very unwell — these can be signs of sepsis.

citations.section: Urinary tract infection (lower) — women, pregnant / Pyelonephritis — acute

abdo-outcome-orange-pretermlabour.title: Suspected preterm labour (under 37 weeks)
actions: Arrange same-day assessment — speculum or vaginal examination for cervical change per local protocol (e.g. fetal fibronectin/Actim Partus where used).

Discuss antenatal corticosteroids for fetal lung maturation, and magnesium sulfate for fetal neuroprotection if very preterm — VERIFY exact gestation cut-offs and dosing locally before giving specifics.
Consider tocolysis and in-utero transfer if the local unit lacks appropriate neonatal cot capacity for the gestation — per local network pathway.
abdo-outcome-orange-pretermlabour.phoneScript: Tell her this needs checking today, this could be early labour and needs assessment now — please come in.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately, any time, if bleeding starts, waters break, or pains become more frequent or severe.

citations.section: Preterm labour and birth — assessment and management of suspected preterm labour

abdo-outcome-yellow-termlabour.title: Possible labour at term (37+ weeks)
abdo-outcome-yellow-termlabour.target: Seen within 1 hour (face-to-face) / advice on timing to attend (phone)
actions: For phone contacts: give standard advice on when to come in (e.g. regular strong contractions roughly every 3–5 minutes lasting 45–60 seconds, or waters breaking, or any bleeding) — VERIFY exact local admission criteria, as these vary by unit and parity.
For face-to-face: assess contraction pattern, offer examination for progress per local pathway, confirm fetal wellbeing.
abdo-outcome-yellow-termlabour.phoneScript: Explain what to watch for and when to come in — strong, regular contractions close together, waters breaking, or any bleeding. Come in sooner if worried at any point.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately, any time, if waters break, there is any bleeding, movements reduce, or she is worried for any reason.

citations.section: Intrapartum care — latent phase advice and admission criteria (actively updated guideline — check current version)

abdo-outcome-orange-preeclampsia-overlap.title: Possible pre-eclampsia — overlapping symptoms
abdo-outcome-orange-preeclampsia-overlap.target: Seen within 15 minutes (face-to-face) / attend within the hour (phone)
actions: This overlaps with the pre-eclampsia screen — work through the Headache, visual disturbance or epigastric pain pathway for full BP-banded guidance.
In the meantime, arrange same-day blood pressure and urine protein check, plus pre-eclampsia bloods (FBC, U&E, LFTs) and fetal assessment (CTG).
abdo-outcome-orange-preeclampsia-overlap.phoneScript: Tell her these symptoms together need checking today — please come in so we can check her blood pressure and take some bloods.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately, any time, if visual disturbance worsens, pain becomes severe, or she feels unwell before her appointment.

citations.section: Hypertension in pregnancy — symptomatic screening for pre-eclampsia

abdo-outcome-green-spd.title: Likely pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain (symphysis pubis dysfunction)
abdo-outcome-green-spd.target: Non-urgent — advice, physiotherapy referral, and safety-netting
actions: Reassure that pain over the pubic bone, groin, hips, or lower back, worse with walking, stairs, standing on one leg, or turning over in bed, is common in pregnancy and is usually mechanical (pelvic girdle pain / SPD) rather than a sign of a problem with the baby.
Refer to obstetric/pelvic health physiotherapy for assessment, exercises, and pelvic support belt advice — VERIFY the local referral route and waiting time.
Practical advice: keep knees together when getting in/out of a car or turning in bed, avoid activities that provoke pain (wide-leg movements, standing on one leg to dress), take stairs one at a time.
This is general reassurance, not a formal diagnosis — she should still be seen if the pain changes character or anything below develops.
abdo-outcome-green-spd.phoneScript: Explain this sounds like common pregnancy-related pelvic joint pain, not a sign of a problem with the baby, and that a referral to the physiotherapy team can help with exercises and support. She should contact us again straight away — any time — if the pain becomes severe or one-sided, she notices bleeding, a temperature, feels generally unwell, or is still worried.
safetyNetting: Contact the unit again immediately if the pain becomes severe, constant, or one-sided, bleeding starts, fever develops, or she feels generally unwell.
Come back at any time, however many times, if still worried — this reassurance does not replace being seen if things change.
documentationPrompts: Pain characteristics and what was excluded.

citations.section: Pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain / symphysis pubis dysfunction — general reassurance and physiotherapy referral advice; not a dedicated NICE guideline topic
Antenatal care — advice on common pregnancy symptoms including pelvic/back pain

abdo-outcome-green-constipation.title: Likely constipation
actions: Reassure that constipation is common in pregnancy (related to hormonal effects on the bowel and, later, pressure from the growing uterus) and is not usually a sign of a problem.
Advise increasing fluid and fibre intake and gentle activity; signpost to local/BNF guidance if a laxative is being considered rather than giving medication advice directly.
This is general reassurance, not a formal diagnosis — she should still be seen if the pain changes character or anything below develops.
abdo-outcome-green-constipation.phoneScript: Explain this sounds like constipation, which is very common in pregnancy and usually settles with more fluids, fibre, and gentle movement. She should contact us again straight away — any time — if the pain becomes severe or constant, she notices bleeding, a temperature, feels generally unwell, or is still worried.
safetyNetting: Contact the unit again immediately if pain becomes severe or constant, bleeding starts, fever develops, or she feels generally unwell.
Come back at any time, however many times, if still worried, or if symptoms don't improve with simple measures.

citations.section: Antenatal care — dietary and lifestyle advice for common pregnancy symptoms including constipation

abdo-outcome-green-roundligament.title: Likely round ligament or musculoskeletal pain
actions: Reassure that sharp or aching pain low in the tummy or groin, worse on movement, coughing, or changing position, is commonly round ligament or musculoskeletal stretching pain and is not usually a sign of a problem.
Advise simple measures — rest, gentle movement, warmth; signpost to local/BNF guidance for analgesia in pregnancy rather than giving medication advice directly.
This is general reassurance, not a formal diagnosis — she should still be seen if the pain changes character or anything below develops.
abdo-outcome-green-roundligament.phoneScript: Explain this sounds like simple round ligament or stretching pain, which is very common and not usually a sign of a problem. She should contact us again straight away — any time — if the pain becomes severe or constant, she notices bleeding, a temperature, feels generally unwell, or is still worried.
safetyNetting: Contact the unit again immediately if pain becomes severe or constant, bleeding starts, fever develops, or she feels generally unwell.
Come back at any time, however many times, if still worried — this reassurance does not replace being seen if things change.
documentationPrompts: Pain characteristics and what was excluded.

citations.section: Round ligament / musculoskeletal pain in pregnancy — general reassurance advice; not a dedicated NICE guideline topic

abdo-outcome-yellow-unclear-early.title: Abdominal pain, cause unclear (under 14 weeks)
actions: Red-flag causes screened and not currently present, but the cause is not clearly benign — arrange face-to-face assessment.
Abdominal and (if indicated) pelvic examination, urinalysis, consider ultrasound if pain persists, is severe, or the diagnosis remains unclear.
Reconsider ectopic pregnancy, ovarian cyst accident, and appendicitis if the picture changes.
abdo-outcome-yellow-unclear-early.phoneScript: Tell her this still needs checking today even though nothing sounds like an emergency right now — please come in so we can examine her properly.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately, any time, if pain becomes severe or one-sided, bleeding starts, fever develops, or she feels faint or unwell.

citations.section: Antenatal care — general safety-netting principles for unexplained symptoms

abdo-outcome-yellow-unclear-later.title: Abdominal pain, cause unclear (14+ weeks)
actions: Red-flag causes screened and not currently present, but the cause is not clearly benign — arrange face-to-face assessment.
Abdominal examination, fetal assessment (CTG if appropriate for gestation), urinalysis, BP check.
Reconsider abruption, labour, appendicitis, UTI, ovarian cyst accident, and pre-eclampsia if the picture changes.
abdo-outcome-yellow-unclear-later.phoneScript: Tell her this still needs checking today even though nothing sounds like an emergency right now — please come in so we can examine her and check the baby.
safetyNetting: Come in immediately, any time, if pain becomes severe or constant, bleeding starts, movements reduce, fever develops, or she feels unwell.

citations.section: Antenatal care — general safety-netting principles for unexplained symptoms
